question: What is the role of the variable LBTESTCD in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Lab Test or Examination Short Name (Char, role: Topic). Short name of the measurement, test, or examination described in LBTEST. It can be used as a column name when converting a dataset from a vertical to a horizontal format. The value in LBTESTCD cannot be longer than 8 characters, nor can it start with a number (e.g., "1TEST" is not valid). LBTESTCD cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. Examples: "ALT", "LDH".

question: What does the variable LBTEST contain in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Lab Test or Examination Name (Char, role: Synonym Qualifier). Verbatim name of the test or examination used to obtain the measurement or finding. Note: Any test normally performed by a clinical laboratory is considered a lab test. The value in LBTEST cannot be longer than 40 characters. Examples: "Alanine Aminotransferase", "Lactate Dehydrogenase".

question: Which values does the variable LBCAT take in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Category for Lab Test (Char, role: Grouping Qualifier). Used to define a category of related records across subjects. Examples: "HEMATOLOGY", "URINALYSIS", "CHEMISTRY".

question: What is the purpose of the variable LBSCAT in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Subcategory for Lab Test (Char, role: Grouping Qualifier). A further categorization of a test category. Examples: "DIFFERENTIAL", "COAGULATION", "LIVER FUNCTION", "ELECTROLYTES".

question: What does the variable LBORRES represent in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Result or Finding in Original Units (Char, role: Result Qualifier). Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.

question: Which units does the variable LBORRESU hold in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Original Units (Char, role: Variable Qualifier). Original units in which the data were collected. The unit for LBORRES. Example: "g/L".

question: What is the variable LBORNRLO used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Reference Range Lower Limit in Orig Unit (Char, role: Variable Qualifier). Lower end of reference range for continuous measurement in original units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

question: What is the variable LBORNRHI used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Reference Range Upper Limit in Orig Unit (Char, role: Variable Qualifier). Upper end of reference range for continuous measurement in original units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

question: What does the variable LBSTRESC contain in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Character Result/Finding in Std Format (Char, role: Result Qualifier). Contains the result value for all findings, copied or derived from LBORRES in a standard format or standard units. LBSTRESC should store all results or findings in character format; if results are numeric, they should also be stored in numeric format in LBSTRESN. For example, if a test has results "NONE", "NEG", and "NEGATIVE" in LBORRES and these results effectively have the same meaning, they could be represented in standard format in LBSTRESC as "NEGATIVE". For other examples, see Original and Standardized Results.

question: What is the variable LBSTRESN used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units (Num, role: Result Qualifier). Used for continuous or numeric results or findings in standard format; copied in numeric format from LBSTRESC. LBSTRESN should store all numeric test results or findings.

question: Which units does the variable LBSTRESU hold in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Standard Units (Char, role: Variable Qualifier). Standardized unit used for LBSTRESC or LBSTRESN.

question: What is the variable LBSTNRLO used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Reference Range Lower Limit-Std Units (Num, role: Variable Qualifier). Lower end of reference range for continuous measurements for LBSTRESC/LBSTRESN in standardized units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

question: What is the variable LBSTNRHI used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Reference Range Upper Limit-Std Units (Num, role: Variable Qualifier). Upper end of reference range for continuous measurements in standardized units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

question: What is the variable LBNRIND used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Reference Range Indicator (Char, role: Variable Qualifier). Indicates where the value falls with respect to reference range defined by LBORNRLO and LBORNRHI, LBSTNRLO and LBSTNRHI, or by LBSTNRC. Examples: "NORMAL", "ABNORMAL", "HIGH", "LOW". Sponsors should specify in the study metadata (Comments column in the Define-XML document) whether LBNRIND refers to the original or standard reference ranges and results. LBNRIND is not used to indicate clinical significance.

question: What does the variable LBSPEC describe in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Specimen Type (Char, role: Record Qualifier). Defines the type of specimen used for a measurement. Examples: "SERUM", "PLASMA", "URINE".

question: What does the variable LBMETHOD describe in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Method of Test or Examination (Char, role: Record Qualifier). Method of the test or examination. Examples: "EIA" (enzyme immunoassay), "ELECTROPHORESIS", "DIPSTICK".

question: What does the variable LBANMETH describe in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Analysis Method (Char, role: Record Qualifier). Analysis method applied to obtain a summarized result. Analysis method describes the method of secondary processing applied to a complex observation result (e.g., a calculation used to measure eGFR).

question: What is the variable LBTPTREF used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Time Point Reference (Char, role: Timing). Name of the fixed reference point referred to by LBELTM, LBTPTNUM, and LBTPT. Examples: "PREVIOUS DOSE", "PREVIOUS MEAL".

question: What does the variable LBDTC record in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Date/Time of Specimen Collection (Char, role: Timing). Date/time of specimen collection represented in ISO 8601 character format.

question: What does the variable LBDY record in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Study Day of Specimen Collection (Num, role: Timing). Study day of specimen collection, measured as integer days. Algorithm for calculations must be relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC variable in Demographics. This formula should be consistent across the submission.

question: What is the variable LBFAST used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Fasting Status (Char, role: Record Qualifier). Indicator used to identify fasting status. Examples: "Y", "N".

question: What is the variable LBSTAT used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Completion Status (Char, role: Record Qualifier). Used to indicate exam not done. Should be null if a result exists in LBORRES.

question: What is the variable LBREASND used for in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Reason Test Not Done (Char, role: Record Qualifier). Describes why a measurement or test was not performed. Examples: "BROKEN EQUIPMENT", "SUBJECT REFUSED", or "SPECIMEN LOST". Used in conjunction with LBSTAT when value is "NOT DONE".

question: What does the variable LBNAM identify in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Vendor Name (Char, role: Record Qualifier). The name or identifier of the laboratory that performed the test.

question: What does the variable LBLOINC contain in the LB domain?
reference_answer: LOINC Code (Char, role: Synonym Qualifier). Code for the lab test from the LOINC code system. The sponsor is expected to provide the dictionary name and version used to map the terms utilizing the Define-XML external codelist attributes.

question: What does the variable LBTOXGR record in the LB domain?
reference_answer: Standard Toxicity Grade (Char, role: Record Qualifier). Records toxicity grade value using a standard toxicity scale (e.g., the NCI CTCAE). If value is from a numeric scale, represent only the number (e.g., "2" not "Grade 2"). The sponsor is expected to provide the name of the scale and version used to map the terms, utilizing the external codelist element in the Define-XML document.

question: What is the structure of the LB dataset and what does it contain?
reference_answer: Laboratory Test Results (class: Findings). Structure: One record per lab test per time point per visit per subject

question: What is the MB dataset used for?
reference_answer: Microbiology Specimen (class: Findings). Structure: One record per microbiology specimen finding per time point per visit per subject

question: What is the MS dataset used for?
reference_answer: Microbiology Susceptibility (class: Findings). Structure: One record per microbiology susceptibility test (or other organism-related finding) per organism found in MB

question: What is the structure of the CP dataset?
reference_answer: Cell Phenotype Findings (class: Findings). Structure: One record per test per specimen per timepoint per visit per subject

question: What is the GF dataset used for?
reference_answer: Genomics Findings (class: Findings). Structure: One record per finding per observation per biospecimen per subject

question: What is the IS dataset used for?
reference_answer: Immunogenicity Specimen Assessments (class: Findings). Structure: One record per test per visit per subject

question: What is the BS dataset used for?
reference_answer: Biospecimen Findings (class: Findings). Structure: One record per measurement per biospecimen identifier per subject

question: What is the PC dataset used for?
reference_answer: Pharmacokinetics Concentrations (class: Findings). Structure: One record per sample characteristic or time-point concentration per reference time point or per analyte per subject

question: What does the variable STUDYID identify in SDTM?
reference_answer: Study Identifier (Char, role: Identifier). A sequence of characters used by the sponsor to uniquely identify the study.

question: What does the variable DOMAIN contain in SDTM?
reference_answer: Domain Abbreviation (Char, role: Identifier). An abbreviation for a collection of observations, with a topic-specific commonality.

question: What is the variable USUBJID used for in SDTM?
reference_answer: Unique Subject Identifier (Char, role: Identifier). A sequence of characters used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product.

question: What is the variable --SEQ used for in SDTM?
reference_answer: Sequence Number (Num, role: Identifier). A number used in combination with the identifier of the subject of the observation to uniquely identify a record within a domain.

question: What does the variable --TESTCD contain in SDTM?
reference_answer: Short Name of Measurement, Test, or Exam (Char, role: Topic). The standardized or dictionary-derived short sequence of characters used to represent the measurement, test, or examination.

question: What is the variable --CAT used for in SDTM?
reference_answer: Category (Char, role: Grouping Qualifier). A grouping or classification of the topic of the finding, event, or intervention.

question: What does the variable --ORRES contain in SDTM?
reference_answer: Result or Finding in Original Units (Char, role: Result Qualifier). The result of the measurement, test, or examination, as originally received or collected.

question: What is the variable --ORRESU used for in SDTM?
reference_answer: Original Units (Char, role: Variable Qualifier). The unit of measure for the result (as originally received or collected) of the measurement, test, or examination.

question: What is the variable --STAT used for in SDTM?
reference_answer: Completion Status (Char, role: Record Qualifier).

question: What does the variable --DTC record in SDTM?
reference_answer: Date/Time of Collection (Char, role: Timing). The date or date and time of the assessment or the specimen or data collection from the subject, represented in a standardized character format.

question: What is the variable --DY used for in SDTM?
reference_answer: Study Day of Visit/Collection/Exam (Num, role: Timing). The number of days from the sponsor-defined reference start date to the date of collection (--DTC), used in study data tabulation.

question: What is the variable --BLFL used for in SDTM?
reference_answer: Baseline Flag (Char, role: Record Qualifier). An indication that the record is the sponsor-defined baseline assessment, used in study data tabulation.
